subject: English Language
source: CISCE ICSE English Language (Paper 1) 2024 - Analysis of Pupil Performance (raw/LangPPA-24.pdf)

marking_schemes.question_text:
Write a composition (300 - 350 words) on the following:
Write an original short story entitled 'A Strange Visitor'.
marking_schemes.scheme_text: The story must be original and must have at least two characters - the narrator and the visitor. The 'strangeness' must be qualified, the encounter and the action that arises out of the encounter described. Credit to be given for humour or suspense. Accept a wide interpretation of visitor as in alien, animal or human.
key_points: Original story with at least two characters: the narrator and the visitor
The 'strangeness' of the visitor is qualified
The encounter and the action arising from it are described
Wide interpretation of 'visitor' accepted (alien, animal or human)
common_errors: Strangeness of the visitor not shown
Wrote a narrative essay, not a story
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Many did not highlight the visitor's 'strangeness' or understand 'strange' as unusual, surprising or unknown. Plot and characters were underdeveloped; twists and dialogue were absent. Most treated it as a narrative essay of a past experience; many did not understand 'original'.

assessment_criteria: Relevance to the chosen topic and every part of the task addressed
Expression: vocabulary, sentence structure, grammar, spelling and punctuation

marking_schemes.question_text:
Write a composition (300 - 350 words) on the following:
Narrate an incident from your experience in which your parents had entrusted you with a difficult task. Give details of the task, how you carried it out and your feelings at the end.
marking_schemes.scheme_text: This is a first-person account and must be narrated from within the plausible experience of a Class X candidate. There must be a clear description of the difficult task and how it was carried out. The feeling of satisfaction, contentment and joy etc. must form the conclusion of the composition.
key_points: First-person account within the plausible experience of a Class X candidate
Clear description of the difficult task
How the task was carried out
Concludes with feelings at the end (satisfaction, contentment, joy etc.)
common_errors: Adult task beyond a Class X student's experience
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Most did not answer the whole question, especially the ending. Many did not understand 'entrusted'; feelings at the end were mostly missing. Many went beyond their plausible age, describing adult tasks such as office work. Sentence structure and language were below the expected standard.

assessment_criteria: Relevance to the chosen topic and every part of the task addressed
Expression: vocabulary, sentence structure, grammar, spelling and punctuation

marking_schemes.question_text:
Write a composition (300 - 350 words) on the following:
Describe how you spend your time on a holiday afternoon. Why do you think it is necessary to have these times of quietness and solitude?
marking_schemes.scheme_text: This is a descriptive essay giving an account of quietness, rest, solitude or a leisure time activity that is done alone like reading, writing, listening to music. The candidate must describe the activity as well as the benefits of quietness and solitude. Any contradiction (e.g. noisy parties, crowds, sports) of solitude and quietness must be penalised.
key_points: Describes a quiet, solitary afternoon activity (e.g. reading, writing, listening to music)
Explains the benefits of quietness and solitude
No contradiction of solitude (noisy parties, crowds, sports are penalised)
common_errors: Described the whole day instead of an afternoon
Ignored or contradicted quietness and solitude
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Many described the whole day or holiday rather than an afternoon. 'Quietness and solitude' were misunderstood or left out; many wrote about enjoyment with friends and relatives.

assessment_criteria: Relevance to the chosen topic and every part of the task addressed
Expression: vocabulary, sentence structure, grammar, spelling and punctuation
penalised: Contradicting solitude and quietness (noisy parties, crowds, sports)

marking_schemes.question_text:
Write a composition (300 - 350 words) on the following:
Express your views either for or against the statement 'Junk food should be banned'.
marking_schemes.scheme_text: Views either for or against are to be accepted. The candidate should take a clear stand and give valid reasons for whatever stand he/she takes. Credit to be given for a cohesive well-constructed logical argument and ideas based on logical reasoning and personal experience.
key_points: Takes one clear stand, either for or against
Cohesive, logical argument drawing on reasoning and personal experience
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Most took a stand against the motion but then described the ill effects of junk food, contradicting themselves. Some repeated arguments, did not take a clear stand, or argued both sides; irrelevant arguments and a lack of illustrative examples were seen.

assessment_criteria: Relevance to the chosen topic and every part of the task addressed
Expression: vocabulary, sentence structure, grammar, spelling and punctuation

marking_schemes.question_text:
Write a composition (300 - 350 words) on the following:
Study the picture given below. Write a story or a description or an account of what it suggests to you. Your composition may be about the subject of the picture, or you may take suggestions from it; however, there must be a clear connection between the picture and your composition.
marking_schemes.scheme_text: Accept a wide interpretation. Any relevant ideas taken from the picture should be accepted. However, a mere itemization / listing / description of the picture is to be penalised.
key_points: Clear connection between the picture and the composition
Wide interpretation accepted: story, description or account
Not a mere itemisation/listing/description of the picture
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Not attempted by many. A few wrote about cricket or other games instead of carrom; some copied the comprehension; mere itemisation was observed, and there was often no clear connection between composition and picture.

assessment_criteria: Relevance to the chosen topic and every part of the task addressed
Expression: vocabulary, sentence structure, grammar, spelling and punctuation
penalised: Mere itemisation / listing / description of the picture

marking_schemes.question_text: Your friend was absent from school on a day when an unfortunate incident took place for which you were blamed. Write a letter to your friend giving details about the incident, your role in it and how the matter was finally resolved.
marking_schemes.scheme_text:
Format (Friendly/Informal letter)
Content
Details about the incident (a 'normal' event where something goes wrong): e.g. a game or classroom activity in which a prank is played / an accident / cheating / any act of misconduct or indiscipline (Any two)
Your role in it: e.g. assisted in the prank / you could be the ringleader / you accidentally or deliberately hurt somebody / copied or assisted in copying / bullying (Any two)
How the problem was resolved: e.g. confession / apology / will not do it again / learnt a lesson (Any one)
Expression: Language, syntax and vocabulary.
key_points: Details about the incident (a 'normal' event where something goes wrong) (any two): e.g. a game or classroom activity in which a prank is played / an accident / cheating / any act of misconduct or indiscipline
Your role in it (any two): e.g. assisted in the prank / you could be the ringleader / you accidentally or deliberately hurt somebody / copied or assisted in copying / bullying
How the problem was resolved (any one): e.g. confession / apology / will not do it again / learnt a lesson
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Many did not understand the whole question, focusing on the incident and how they were blamed; proving innocence and their role were often not described, and the resolution was sometimes missing. Some wrote about incidents outside school. Format: punctuation, 'February' spelling, wrong/missing year, 'Yours sincerely' subscription, ABC/XYZ signatures, 'Dear friend' without a name. Expression: spelling, grammar and sentence structure errors.

format_elements: Date (day, month written in full, year)
Salutation addressing the recipient by name or relation (e.g. Dear Riya / Dear Grandma)
Body: opening sentence, content paragraphs, closing sentence
Subscription (e.g. Yours lovingly / Yours affectionately), no apostrophe in 'Yours'

content_requirements.element: Details about the incident (a 'normal' event where something goes wrong)
examples: a game or classroom activity in which a prank is played
any act of misconduct or indiscipline
you accidentally or deliberately hurt somebody

marking_schemes.question_text: You wish to stage a play to create awareness about the importance of saving electricity. Write a letter to the Manager of a nearby shopping mall/supermarket requesting permission to use the space in front of the shopping mall/supermarket to stage the play. Give him/her details about your requirements and state why the play will be beneficial to the shoppers.
marking_schemes.scheme_text:
Format (Formal letter)
Content
Request permission: e.g. Please may I / kindly grant
Details about requirement: e.g. date / time / other arrangements like stage, electricity, microphones
Why the play will be beneficial: e.g. conservation of resources / overuse of fossil fuels / creating awareness of the need to conserve
Expression: Language, syntax and vocabulary.
key_points: Request permission: e.g. Please may I / kindly grant
Details about requirement: e.g. date / time / other arrangements like stage, electricity, microphones
Why the play will be beneficial: e.g. conservation of resources / overuse of fossil fuels / creating awareness of the need to conserve
common_errors: Mall name missing from receiver's address
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Format: incomplete sender's address; name of the mall missing from the receiver's address; 'February' errors; 'Respected Sir', 'Yours sincerely', 'ABC'/'XYZ'. Content: weight went to benefits; requirements were neglected - many named only 'space' without specifics. Expression: punctuation, spelling, grammar, paragraphing errors; informal language such as 'we are kids'.

writing_task.recipient: The Manager of a shopping mall/supermarket
format_elements: Date (day, month written in full, year)
Receiver's address beginning with the designation, then organisation and city
Salutation (Sir / Madam / Dear Sir / Dear Madam), not 'Respected Sir'
Body: opening sentence, content paragraphs, closing sentence

examples: other arrangements like stage, electricity, microphones

content_requirements.element: Why the play will be beneficial
examples: creating awareness of the need to conserve

marking_schemes.question_text: Your school is hosting an Inter School Dance Competition. Write a notice to be put up on your school notice board informing the students about the event.
marking_schemes.scheme_text:
Creative Title: Rhythmic Beats / Twinkletoes / Happy Feet
Event: Inter School Dance Competition
Date: Accept single date, for example a week or fortnight away from the date of writing
Time: 10.00 a.m. - 3.00 p.m.
Venue: smaller place to larger
Participation: All pupils who wish to register should give their names to the Vice Principal/etc. on or before ...
key_points: Creative Title: Rhythmic Beats / Twinkletoes / Happy Feet
Date: Accept single date, for example a week or fortnight away from the date of writing
Participation: All pupils who wish to register should give their names to the Vice Principal/etc. on or before ...
common_errors: Event date unrealistic or year missing
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Creative titles were missing, used words naming the event, were irrelevant or too long. Event dates coincided with the exam, lacked the year, or were too far ahead (should be about 10-14 days after the notice). Details were written as a paragraph; date, time and venue were interchanged or incomplete. Registration dates were too close to or after the event.

examples: Accept single date, for example a week or fortnight away from the date of writing
All pupils who wish to register should give their names to the Vice Principal/etc. on or before ...

penalised: Words from the question used in the creative title (recommended against)

Subject
Salutation
Opening sentence
Closing sentence
Subscription

key_points: E-mail id (recipient; official, with @ and provider)
Expression - All details of the notice are to be included in the e-mail.

stimulus.text:
Ashamanja Babu lived in a small flat in Bhowanipore. A clerk in the registry department of Lajpat Rai Post Office, Ashamanja Babu was fortunate as he could walk to his office in seven minutes flat without having to fight his way into the buses and trains of Calcutta. He lived a rather carefree life as he was not the kind of person to sit and brood about what might have been had Fate been kinder to him. On the whole, he was quite content with his lot. Two Hindi films and fish twice a week - these were enough to keep him happy. The only thing that perturbed him at times was his lack of companionship. A bachelor with few friends and relatives, he often wished he had a dog to keep him company. It need not be a huge Alsatian like the one owned by the Talukdars, who lived two houses down the lane; it could be any ordinary little dog which would follow him around morning and evening, wag its tail when he came home from work and obey his orders faithfully. Ashamanja Babu's secret desires were that he would speak to his dog in English. 'Stand up', 'Sit down', 'Shake hands' - how nice it would be if his dog obeyed such commands! That would make him really happy.

On a cloudy day marked by a steady drizzle, Ashamanja Babu went to the market in Hashimara to buy some oranges. At one end of the market, beside a stunted kul tree, sat a man. As their eyes met, the man smiled. Was he a beggar? His clothes made him look like one. Ashamanja Babu noticed at least five sewn-on patches on his trousers and jacket. But the man didn't have a begging bowl. Instead, by his side was a shoe-box with a little pup sticking its head out of it.

'Good morning!' said the man in English. Ashamanja Babu was obliged to return the greeting.

'Buy dog? Dog buy? Very good dog.' The man had taken the pup out of the box and had put it down on the ground. 'Very cheap. Very good. Happy dog.'

The pup shook the raindrops off its coat, looked at Ashamanja Babu and wagged its minuscule two-inch tail. Ashamanja Babu moved closer to the pup, crouched on the ground and stretched out his hand. The pup gave his ring finger a lick with its pink tongue. Nice, friendly dog.

'How much? What price?'

'Ten rupees.'

A little haggling and the price came down to seven rupees. Ashamanja Babu paid the money, put the pup back in the shoe-box, closed the lid to save it from the drizzle, and turned homewards, forgetting all about the oranges.
stimulus.source: Ashamanja Babu's Dog by Satyajit Ray
stimulus.line_references: Line numbers in questions refer to the printed paper's margin numbering.

The pup shook the raindrops off its coat, looked at Ashamanja Babu and wagged its minuscule two-inch tail. Ashamanja Babu moved closer to the pup, crouched on the ground and stretched out his hand. The pup gave his ring finger a lick with its pink tongue. Nice, friendly dog.

'How much? What price?'

'Ten rupees.'

A little haggling and the price came down to seven rupees. Ashamanja Babu paid the money, put the pup back in the shoe-box, closed the lid to save it from the drizzle, and turned homewards, forgetting all about the oranges.

stimulus.text:
Ashamanja Babu lived in a small flat in Bhowanipore. A clerk in the registry department of Lajpat Rai Post Office, Ashamanja Babu was fortunate as he could walk to his office in seven minutes flat without having to fight his way into the buses and trains of Calcutta. He lived a rather carefree life as he was not the kind of person to sit and brood about what might have been had Fate been kinder to him. On the whole, he was quite content with his lot. A bachelor with few friends and relatives, he often wished he had a dog to keep him company. Ashamanja Babu's secret desires were that he would speak to his dog in English. 'Stand up', 'Sit down', 'Shake hands' - how nice it would be if his dog obeyed such commands! 'How much? What price?'

'Ten rupees.'

A little haggling and the price came down to seven rupees. Ashamanja Babu paid the money, put the pup back in the shoe-box, closed the lid to save it from the drizzle, and turned homewards, forgetting all about the oranges.

marking_schemes.question_text: In not more than 50 words, narrate the series of events from the time the puppy was taken out of the box till it was paid for.
marking_schemes.scheme_text:
Points:

marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Many exceeded 50 words, dropped articles to cut the count, or summarised the whole passage. marking_schemes.question_text:
Fill in each of the numbered blanks with the correct form of the word given in brackets. Do not copy the passage but write in correct serial order the word or phrase appropriate to the blank space.
Example: Next day my uncle (0) ______ (spend) a lot of time. Answer: (0) spent
He (1) ______ (select) clothes for me, and my aunt (2) ______ (give) my face a scrub and (3) ______ (groom) me. My uncle (4) ______ (follow) me about (5) ______ (utter) several pieces of advice before (6) ______ (let) me out. 'You must never scowl even if the sun (7) ______ (hit) you in the eyes. You must try (8) ______ (look) pleasant.'
marking_schemes.scheme_text: [0. spent] (1) selected  (2) gave  (3) groomed  (4) followed  (5) uttered / uttering  (6) letting  (7) hits  (8) to look
marking_schemes.model_answer:
(1) selected
(2) gave
(3) groomed
(4) followed
(5) uttered
(6) letting
(7) hits
(8) to look
common_errors: Present tense for past (selects, follows, utters)
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Common errors: (1) selects/select/'selets', (2) give/'gaves', (3) grooms/'gromed', (4) follows, (5) utters, (6) lets, (7) heats/hit/'hites', (8) looking. Some gave two answers.

1: Stress originality; teach plot structure, dialogue, character building and logical endings
Explain the difference between a short story and a first-person account
Ensure each sub-part of the question is answered without overlap
Use precise language, vivid detail and figurative language in descriptions
For argument: strong stance, three or four main points with examples; conduct class debates
Use the picture as a precursor to the composition; avoid itemisation
2: Teach correct format (address, date, salutation, subscription) via CISCE's website
Read the question carefully and develop every point; identify key elements (event, requirements, benefits)
Avoid contractions, short forms and colloquial language
3: Refer to www.cisce.org for format; practise two-to-three-word creative titles
Event date 10-14 days after the notice; gap between registration and event
Distinguish personal and official email ids; copy the event as the email subject
Notice and email date, time and venue must correspond
4: Dictionary work, word games, synonyms and homonyms
Use own words rather than copying
Keep summaries within 50 words, in sequence, without dropping articles
5: Teach tense changes and spelling of verb forms
Write one option and match letter to statement
Revise question tags, voice, too/so, not only, rather...than, reported speech, inversion after 'Never'

difficult_topics: Q1(i): short scripts or overlong compositions
Q2 & Q3: formats of letter, notice and email
Q4(iv): higher-order questions and summary writing
Tense usage, punctuation, spelling, singular/plural, articles, conjunctions
confusions: Identifying a question as factual/text-based or analytical
